newsitem.title: UK: BT to face investor pressure over MCI - papers.
newsitem.headline: BT to face investor pressure over MCI - papers.

text.p: Institutional investors have warned British Telecommunications Plc that they will block its $24 billion merger with MCI unless the deal is is renegotiated, UK newspapers said on Sunday.
The pressure from shareholders follows a profit warning from MCI, America's second biggest long-distance carrier, on Thursday.
Investors are concerned not only about BT paying too much for the deal but that the drain on the company's cashflow will dampen prospects for dividend growth.
The Sunday Times also said investors will pushing BT to renegotiate the deal. The rationale for the merger remained but the British company was likely to take a closer look at the costs involved.

BT has set up a special task force and is prepared to send its own personnel into senior positions at MCI to scrutinise its finances and to find out how losses spiraled out of control, the Independent on Sunday said.

The Sunday Telegraph said two of MCI's most senior managers were expected to come under pressure to resign as a result of the losses - Doug Maine, MCI's finance director and Tim Price, head of telecoms business.

Traders wiped over two billion pounds ($3.4 billion) off BT's market value on Friday following MCI's warning late on Thursday that losses due to heavy investments in local markets would be more than twice forecast this year. MCI said those losses could reach $800 million - and could be even higher next year. BT was unavailable for comment. -- London newsroom + 44 171 542 7717
